phase07_dense_few_shot_sweep._note_schema: Deliberately NOT nested under `configs.*`: BaselineConfig.cases is a REQUIRED dict[str,bool] field, and this sweep captured only aggregate pass-rates + a single fresh McNemar pairing per test (no per-case verdict dicts across all N=5 runs, per the human's paste-back). Inventing a per-case `cases` map to satisfy the schema would fabricate data, so the sweep is folded in here as a sibling top-level key instead of a `configs['openai-gpt4o-mini-dense']`-style entry. Full narrative in 07-04-SUMMARY.md.

provenance.resolved_model_snapshot_ids_note: NOT captured this sweep (limitation). The dense-vs-committed-0.32 (06.2) continuity check is therefore INAPPLICABLE/INVALID here -- 06.2's resolved snapshot is also unrecorded, so no snapshot-equality claim can be made either way.

primary_confirmatory_test.description: PRE-REGISTERED confirmatory test (M1/M2/B1): gpt-4o-mini anchor, dense vs a freshly-run zero arm, PAIRED McNemar over the same 25 cases, same session. Lift PASSES iff p<0.05. This is THE single confirmatory bar for NL-FEW-02.
primary_confirmatory_test.mde_context: At n=25 and base-rate ~0.32 the paired design detects roughly a 4-case (~16pt) lift at p<0.05. This is a documented 'cannot-confirm-at-n=25' null interpreted against that MDE, NOT proof of no effect.
primary_confirmatory_test.nl_few_02_disposition: Closed via the plan-sanctioned human-accepted-documented-null completion path -- explicitly NOT a passed confirmatory test.

secondary_bm25_vs_zero_gpt4o_mini.description: SECONDARY/exploratory: bm25 was a pre-specified arm, but this specific comparison (bm25-vs-zero) was post-hoc, not the pre-registered confirmatory test. Report as secondary -- do not relabel as THE confirmatory result.

exploratory_dense_vs_zero_gpt5.verdict: null (point estimate +16pt, not significant at n=25)

key_findings: The pre-registered confirmatory test (dense vs zero, gpt-4o-mini) is a documented NULL (p=0.453) interpreted against the ~16pt MDE -- a cannot-confirm-at-n=25 null, not proof of no effect. NL-FEW-02 closes via the human-accepted documented-null path, not a passed confirmatory test.

Lexical BM25 >= dense embeddings in EVERY tier (gpt-4o-mini 0.568>0.504; gpt-5-mini 0.440>0.296; gpt-5 0.552>0.496) -- contradicts the phase's founding SOTA-survey thesis that dense ranks #1. Genuine finding, not a failure.

SECONDARY significant result: gpt-4o-mini bm25-vs-zero IS significant (p=0.0312, 6/0 favorable flips, 0.376->0.568 = +19pt) -- reported as secondary/exploratory since bm25-vs-zero was post-hoc; the confirmatory verdict stays the dense null.

Default-install story (M3): production .[nl] is torch-free and uses BM25; the significant lift rides on the DEFAULT install. Dense's extra weight (torch/sentence-transformers) did not pay off at this bank size.
gpt-4o-mini zero-shot (0.376) beat both gpt-5 tiers' zero-shot (0.24-0.26) -- observation only, likely reasoning-model output-shape vs judge strictness, not over-interpreted.
limitations: Only aggregate pass-rates + a single fresh-pairing McNemar test per comparison were captured and pasted back -- NOT full per-case verdict dicts across all N=5 runs per (model, arm). This is why this sweep is recorded here rather than as configs['*-dense']/['*-bm25'] BaselineConfig entries (which require a per-case `cases` map).

Resolved dated model snapshot ids for the gpt-4o-mini/gpt-5-mini/gpt-5 bare aliases were NOT captured this sweep. The M2 dense-vs-committed-0.32 (06.2) continuity check is therefore inapplicable/invalid -- 06.2's resolved snapshot is also unrecorded.
